To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) decision makers who are supported by high levels of analytics expertise and analytics elaboration, but do not have the ability to understand the analytics, will not use analytic advice, (2) decision makers who have the ability to process the analytics will use it and (3) decision makers who use the analytic advice will make higher-quality decisions.
the quality of BI&A support, the decision makers’ systematic information processing, and the trustworthiness in their analytics experts are all relevant to decision quality.

the quality of decisions is influenced by the extent of analytics elaboration, decision makers’ systematic information processing and the adoption of analytic recommendations, as well as the trustworthiness of the analytics expert.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how BI&A can be leveraged for improving decision quality, and how this depends on the characteristics of decision makers’ information search and processing behavior.
the question of how to improve BI&A support to increase decision quality.
the effects of BI&A on decision processes, and how this ultimately contributes to the quality of decisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of BI&A on decision quality are contingent upon the decision maker’s processing modes.
the more analytics are elaborated, the less decision makers process information systematically and the more they rely on heuristics.
the quality of decision making processes is not only dependent on BI&A technology, and that the decision maker’s characteristics and behavior also play a key role.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the utilization of BI&A support can be improved by a more systematic processing of information, while heuristic processing should be avoided.
the quality of BI&A-supported decision making is not only determined by the quality of BI&Asupport, but also by the characteristics of the decision makers’ information processes.
the utilization of BI&A support is not a simple matter of “the more, the better.”
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quality of BI&A decisions is not only determined by BI&A support and the decision maker’s processing behavior, but also depends on the interaction between the two.
decision makers’ systematic information processing is a critical factor for decision quality and that analytics experts can positively contribute to the adoption of analytic information.

the quality of decision makers’ information-processing behavior is an essential factor for improving decision quality in BI&A-supported decisions, and it can be influenced by the level of analytics elaboration and analytics expertise.
